narrative.overview: Every change arrives tagged like a triage case: a tag that pairs a printed color band with a numeral and a word, a banded chart that shows which observation forced the escalation, and a handover of what is still uncertain. Cool form paper under ink-navy text; color reserved for the one action ink, the triage bands and verdicts.
keyCharacteristics: Die-cut lane tags with a punched hole, numeral and word: never color alone.
Banded observation chart (lane columns tinted, hairline armature) explains every lane.
Three verdict shapes: filled disc with check, dashed ring, triangle.
One family (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next) for all UI; its Mono sibling only for code, hashes and data.
Hairline-separated rows instead of cards; panels only where a block is one decision.
On the landing, the same world at poster scale: a case tag whose signed evidence tears off the review it proves.

rules.name: The Band Means Lane Rule
rules.body: Carmine, ochre and green appear only as lane, verdict or state, and always beside a numeral, word or shape that says the same thing.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Teal marks the primary action, links, the current selection and focus. If a count, a status or a secondary button is teal, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Unknown Is Not Green Rule
rules.body: A skipped or failed measurement renders in ochre or carmine with the words Not measured or Measurement failed.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for code, hashes, versions, globs and commands only.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No tracked all-caps labels and no kicker above a heading.

rules.name: The Edge Or Lift Rule
rules.body: A container has a hairline edge or a raise, not both; decision panels carry a 2px ink edge.

rules.name: The Torn Strip Rule
rules.body: A strip still attached is review still owed, printed in its lane's full band with the band's edge on its perforation. A strip the evidence tore off drops to its lane's tint behind a torn edge and hangs rotated 3 to 4 degrees below the tag. The loudest thing on the tag is always what a person still has to do.

dos: Do pair every lane, verdict and test outcome with a word, numeral or shape (the Band Means Lane Rule).
Do keep tour prose at 1.0625rem with a 68ch measure, and put the reviewer agent's least-confident and not-done lists before the stops on a neutral surface with a 3px ink top rule.
Do make signing deliberate: name the consequence, gate on an explicit attestation where the act is a plan approval, wait for the server, and say what was recorded.
Do use tabular numerals for counts, percentages, times and line numbers.
Do keep primary phone actions in the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding.
Do show product screens on the landing at 1:1 with light, dark and phone-width captures, and label demo data where it is seen.
Do make every landing copy control work without script: the value is selectable text first, the copy button an enhancement.
donts: Don't encode a lane as a colored side stripe on a card or row; use the tag and the tinted group band.
Don't use monospace for names, labels or prose ids.
Don't put a kicker or tracked uppercase label above a heading.
Don't show a pulsing live dot; live data is shown as a ticking countdown or a checked N seconds ago line.
Don't let anything but code blocks and rails scroll horizontally.
Don't spend motion anywhere except state feedback and the approval seal (on the landing, the case tag's one load moment).
